proposals.impact: title reads like a forum question, not a post worth clicking
proposals.observation: The blog post "Would charging for energy healing be a form of good or bad Karma and why do think so?" was published 26 Sep and immediately reverted once before being reapplied (commits c69ac0f and dbd60fa). The title is a verbatim copy of a Quora question. That format performs poorly in email previews and search snippets because it signals "someone else's question" rather than "Joel's answer." The grammar error ("why do think so") makes it worse. The ICP for this post — energy healers anxious about pricing their work — is exactly right. The topic has real pull. The title is the only thing letting it down.
proposals.proposal: Rewrite the post title and the frontmatter slug-display title so it reads as Joel's considered position, not a forum prompt. The body stays untouched. The file path stays untouched (slug is already committed and 301s are in place). Change only the `title:` line in frontmatter.
proposals.current_text: title: "Would charging for energy healing be a form of good or bad Karma and why do think so?"
proposals.new_text: title: "Charging for energy healing is not a moral failing — it is what keeps healers healing"

proposals.impact: open rate 37.5% is 15+ points below Money Vigilance — a subject line test could close the gap fast
proposals.observation: Money Worship automation: 16 sent, 6 opens, 37.5% open rate. Money Vigilance: 12 sent, 8 opens, 66.67%. Money Avoidance sits in the middle at 52.63%. The 29-point gap between Worship and Vigilance is too large to explain by audience quality alone at these send volumes. The most likely culprit is the subject line for the Worship sequence — either it reads as generic self-improvement copy, or it triggers a "I already know this about myself" skip. Money Vigilance subscribers are probably opening because the subject line names something they feel but have not seen named clearly before. The Worship sequence needs the same specificity.
proposals.proposal: Rewrite the subject line for email 1 of the WoW - Money Worship automation. The goal is to name the specific, uncomfortable thing Money Worship subscribers actually do — spending as proof of worth, or equating net worth with self-worth — so they feel seen rather than categorised. One sentence, no question mark (questions invite "maybe later"), no banned words.
proposals.current_text: subject: "Money Worship: what your score really means"
proposals.new_text: subject: "You earned it, so why does spending it feel like proof you deserve to exist"

proposals.impact: 0 sessions in 48h means no one is finding the quiz entry point
proposals.observation: The quiz shows 0 sessions and 0 starts across a 48-hour window. Every automation in MailerLite is active and sending, which means subscribers are arriving through some route — but not through the quiz. The domain move (thewayofwealth.shop to wayofwealthcoaching.com) landed yesterday. It is possible the quiz entry point on the homepage or the navigation still carries the old domain in its href, or the quiz CTA was not updated in the homepage restructure (commit 8a7e6ed, "Homepage + /coaching structure from lasting competitor pages"). Zero quiz traffic with live automations suggests the funnel's top has a broken or invisible door.
proposals.proposal: Audit the homepage hero CTA and the navigation link that point to the quiz. Confirm the href resolves to wayofwealthcoaching.com/quiz/ (not the old .shop domain) and that the CTA button is present in the rendered HTML above the fold. If the href is stale, update it. This is a one-line fix if the redirect missed the quiz path, or a one-element fix if the CTA was dropped during the homepage restructure.
